steps: Allotropy is the existence of an element in two or more different forms in the same physical state. These forms have different physical properties but similar chemical properties.
Carbon exists in crystalline forms, such as diamond and graphite, and in amorphous forms, such as coal, charcoal and coke.
Diamond has a regular arrangement of carbon atoms. It is extremely hard, transparent and a good conductor of heat but a poor conductor of electricity.
Graphite has carbon atoms arranged in layers. It is soft and slippery and conducts electricity.
Sulphur exists in three allotropic forms: rhombic sulphur, monoclinic sulphur and plastic sulphur.

Rhombic sulphur is yellow and crystalline and is stable at ordinary temperatures. Monoclinic sulphur consists of yellow needle-shaped crystals and is stable at higher temperatures. Plastic sulphur is a dark, rubber-like, non-crystalline form.
Coal is an impure, amorphous form of carbon, whereas diamond is a pure, crystalline form of carbon.
Coal is black and comparatively soft; diamond is transparent and extremely hard.
items.finalAnswer: Carbon and sulphur occur in different allotropic forms; coal is impure amorphous carbon, while diamond is pure crystalline carbon.

steps: A supercritical fluid is a substance above its critical temperature and critical pressure, where the distinction between its liquid and gaseous states disappears.
Unlike an ordinary liquid, a supercritical fluid has no definite surface between liquid and gas and has no surface tension.
It can diffuse through materials like a gas while dissolving substances like a liquid.
items.finalAnswer: A supercritical fluid exists above its critical temperature and pressure and combines gas-like diffusion with liquid-like dissolving ability.
